history.summary: Arulmigu Koniamman Temple on Big Bazaar Street, Town Hall, in the heart of Coimbatore city (CSV town 'Coimbatore' is correct), on the northern bank of the Noyyal river, is one of the twin historic temples of the city (the other being Perur Pateeswarar Temple). Koniamman, a form of Parvati, is the city's guardian deity (Kaaval Deivam); locals begin marriages and new ventures with her blessings. The city's name is popularly derived from the goddess: Koyamma/Kovaiamma → Koyampuththoor → Coimbatore. Wikipedia dates the temple to the 11th century (built by descendants of chieftain Kovan), while other sources call it 600+ years old (Nayak era) or 16th century AD — the built date is disputed (verify). Dravidian architecture; the 7-tiered, 84-ft Rajagopuram was completed in 2011 and is a city landmark. Notable: the Navagrahas are enshrined with their consorts. Administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
